title: Blank COMMON // is shared across the entire program — invisible global state
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PUSH(X)
C     The unnamed COMMON area (just COMMON / / X without a label) is
C     shared across EVERY translation unit that declares it. It is
C     the legacy equivalent of a process-global variable, but it
C     never appears in the subroutine signature -- a reader who
C     skims the args list misses that this routine mutates global
C     state.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL X
      REAL STACK_TOP
      COMMON / / STACK_TOP
      STACK_TOP = X
      RETURN
      END
notes: Blank COMMON is the closest thing legacy Fortran had to a Java static field. The rewrite has to decide: singleton, module-level variable, or inject through the signature? The spec must capture the global-state side effect AND surface the thread-safety question — blank COMMON has no defined concurrency semantics.
